newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian share market slide set to persist.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian share market slide set to persist.

text.p: Nigerian shares finished lower on Friday on sustained offloading of leading stocks, which dealers said would continue for some time.
The all-share index closed at 8409.05 from 8422.76 on Thursday.
Traders said persistent selling of blue chips was forcing prices down steadily.

"Investors are selling because of the perception that shares are adjusting because they are presently considered to be over-priced," one trader said. "The trend will continue in the foreseeable future as large quantities are on offer."
Most conglomerates were on a downturn on Friday after enjoying a brief respite on Thursday.
PZ Industries fell by 10 kobo to 26.20 naira, Lever Brothers was down five kobo 26.45 naira while UAC ended eight kobo less at 15.42 naira.
Food sector shares were also weak. Nestle slid 20 kobo to 52.10 naira on its poor first quarter result.
Nigerian Bottling Co remained in free fall, finishing 20 kobo lower at 52.20 naira while Cadbury closed five down at 35.25 naira.
Oil shares Agip lost 30 kobo to 16.20 naira while Total fell 15 kobo to 57.45 naira.
Speculation moved the few gainers up.
Cappa and D'Alberto appreciated on expectation of a good result, closing 30 kobo higher at 12.90 naira.
UBA, one of the nation's three biggest banks, added seven kobo to 12.97 naira and NAL Merchant Bank rose five kobo to 8.65 naira.
Other five koba gains were posted by Wema Bank at 4.05 naira, brewer Guinness at 7.60 naira, textile group Afprint at 2.50 naira and Mobil at 64.60 naira.
Dealers said Afprint was attractive after posting impressive results recently.
"The stock will remain among the performers in the weeks ahead, although the duration of the rise is conjectural," said one dealer.
